Ben / team — below is a proposed, contract-friendly set of definitions and an alternative remedy ladder that balances operational risk and commercial exposure. I'm keeping measurements tied to telemetry we already emit.

Proposed definitions (for redline):
- "Reserved GPU Bundle": the set of GPUs reserved for Customer under this Agreement (8x A100-equivalent GPUs), accessible as a pooled resource.
- "vGPU-hour": one (1) vGPU-hour equals one hour of active GPU compute time normalized to an A100-40GB baseline. Normalization: measured GPU cycles * architecture factor, reported by the Redwood serving runtime. Billing granularity: 0.01 hour.
- "Throughput Guarantee": the Provider guarantees that the aggregate token throughput for Customer's pool will meet or exceed the Guaranteed Throughput (18,000 tokens/second) at the 95th percentile across rolling 5-minute windows, averaged per calendar day. Measurements will exclude scheduled maintenance windows with 48-hour notice.

Proposed remedies (monthly measurement basis):
- If monthly Availability/Throughput >= 99.5% of Guaranteed Throughput: no credit.
- If 99.0% <= monthly Availability/Throughput < 99.5%: 5% credit of monthly reserved fee.
- If 95.0% <= monthly Availability/Throughput < 99.0%: 15% credit.
- If monthly Availability/Throughput < 95.0%: 30% credit, plus coordinated remediation plan.

Caveats & limits:
- Credit cap: cumulative credits per invoice cycle capped at 50% of that month's reserved fee.
- Cure period: if shortfall is due to Customer misconfiguration or unexpected spikes outside agreed capacity profiles, Redwood will notify and provide a 10-business-day remediation period before credits apply.
- Audit: Customer may request one technical audit per 12 months; audit scope limited to telemetry relevant to measurement definitions; Redwood will provide redacted telemetry exports and a summary report.
- Amortization: unused vGPU-hours may be carried forward for up to 3 full billing cycles (months) and must be used against subsequent consumption; no cash refunds for unused hours.

I'll attach this language as a tracked redline. If legal wants to tighten wording around "normalization" we can add the architecture factor table.

— Dev

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Per our internal review we've consolidated proposed contract language and pushed a small commercial adjustment to address underutilization and audit. Summary of the asks we addressed: definitions, remedy ladder, amortization, audit rights.

Summary (high level):
- Definitions: "vGPU-hour" = normalized A100-40GB compute-hour (0.01 hour granularity); "Throughput Guarantee" = 95th percentile across rolling 5-minute windows, averaged daily.
- Remedies (monthly): >=99.5% = 0; 99.0–99.5% = 5% credit; 95.0–99.0% = 15% credit; <95.0% = 30% credit + remediation plan. Credit cap = 50% of monthly fee.
- Amortization: unused vGPU-hours carry forward up to 3 months. After 3 months unused hours expire. No cash refunds.
- Audit: one audit/year; telemetry export and summary delivered within 7 business days; audit limited to agreed scope.

Commercial concession: we can increase the carry-forward window to 3 months (from standard 1 month) for a 12-month commit. We can also offer a 10% up-front discount on Year 2 if CloudCore signs a 24-month term.

Attached: redwood_term_sheet_cloudcore_20270414.pdf with the updated tables + a DocuSign link to the term sheet. If this looks good to you, we'll prepare a final redline for legal that tracks the exact definition language.

Best,
Ben
